newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dragonair carries record 27-tonne cargo load.
newsitem.headline: Dragonair carries record 27-tonne cargo load.

text.p: Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair) carried a company record cargo load of almost 27 tonnes from the Taiwanese port of Kaohsiung to Hong Kong recently, according the airline's magazine "Kargo News".
One of the carrier's Airbus A330 aircraft uplifted the 26,977 kg of cargo on January 17, nearly half of which was destined for the China capital, Beijing, the latest edition of the magazine said.
Dragonair began three daily flights to Kaohsiung last July.
According to latest statistics from Hong Kong's Civil Aviation Department, Kaohsiung is Dragonair's biggest cargo market for imports to Hong Kong.
A total of 743 tonnes of Kaohsiung-originating cargo was unloaded in Hong Kong while 360 tonnes was flown back to Kaohsiung during February.
Shanghai accounts for the largest amount of cargo exports from Hong Kong on Dragonair, with 530 tonnes flown to the city during February.
Just 31 tonnes was flown by the airline to Hong Kong from Shanghai during the same period.
Dragonair also said it recorded a company cargo uplift record of 7.3 tonnes from the Chinese city of Xiamen to Hong Kong on March 6 using an Airbus A320 aircraft.
Dragonair said it is now offering extra capacity to and from Xiamen on Tuesday and Thursdays, substituting an Airbus A320 with a larger Airbus A330 aircraft to offer cargo agents greater flexibility.

Dragonair does not publish detailed cargo statistics but a graph in the company's newspaper shows the amount of cargo carried during 1996 rose from under 1,000 tonnes in January to just over 3,000 tonnes a month by year end.
